Hi Ariya / Ben —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the p95/p99 targets and what to run for a fair apples-to-apples comparison between your current provider and Redwood hosted API.

Key items we captured on the call:
- Goal: end-to-end user-perceived latency for the text generation pipeline (including client->edge->model->response). You're focusing on p95 and p99 as the primary SLOs.
- Targets: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 600ms for the 256-token average prompt mix (see attached sample distribution).
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline expected steady-state QPS ~120 requests/sec, with concurrency bursts to 400 concurrent streams for short spikes.
- Streaming: you rely on token-level streaming to the client; initial token latency matters for perceived responsiveness.
- Current provider numbers: Ben shared a 4-week export, which shows p95 ~420ms, p99 ~780ms under similar load (attached).

Proposed evaluation plan (we cover details in the attached test plan):
1) Redwood will run a hosted API benchmark using your customer prompt set and token budget, measuring end-to-end p95/p99 across two traffic patterns: steady-state and burst spikes.
2) We'll match model family and quantization/settings as closely as possible; where identical model binaries aren't available we'll document and account for differences.
3) We'll provide streaming traces and per-token timings so you can validate perceived latency improvements.
4) Run two 2-hour windows (steady + burst). We'll deliver results and a quick runbook for integration-specific tuning (batching, prefix caching).

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm the p95/p99 target numbers above (350/600ms) are the priority SLOs we should optimize for?
- Please confirm the sample prompt set we used is representative (attached finlytics-current-metrics-202610.csv).
- Proposed dates: Redwood team runs the benchmark Wed 11/03 in your UTC-8 evening window (we'll coordinate exact window).

Thanks — I copied Aditya and Dylan for technical leads on the Redwood side. We'll share a detailed test plan and a short checklist for any firewall/whitelisting needed.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — good summary and thanks for the thorough plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Targets: yes, p95 <= 350ms and p99 <= 600ms are the targets we need to hit for our web UI flow. Meeting the p99 is more critical since it affects heavy page loads.
- Throughput: the 120 QPS steady-state is accurate. Bursts can get up to 400 concurrent requests for short periods (~2-5 minutes).
- Streaming: token-level streaming is required; we use initial token acknowledgement to render first-line text. If initial token RTT is >150ms it degrades the UX noticeably.

We'll double-check the prompt set and reply if there are any gaps — looks representative from a quick glance.

We can make Wed 11/03 work; please send the exact time and any IPs to whitelist. Also please include in the results a latency breakdown by model step (initial token, subsequent tokens, total) and an end-to-end waterfall so our infra team can correlate.

Cheers,
Ariya
SRE Lead, Finlytics
